basics.name: Alex Fenwick
basics.label: Robotics & Mechanical Engineering Student
basics.summary: I am studying for a B.S. in Robotics Engineering and a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering at Worcester Polytechnic Institute, graduating in May 2027. I most recently worked as a Vehicle Design Intern at SpaceX in Starbase, TX, where I created detail drawings, ran tolerance stack-ups, and wrote GD&T callouts for flight hardware. I care most about the point where mechanical design meets manufacturing.

highlights: Created detail drawings from scratch, defining datum schemes, running tolerance stack-ups, and writing GD&T callouts informed by manufacturer capability.
Used Siemens NX and Teamcenter for CAD modeling and drawing release workflows as part of a larger engineering group.
Completed initial CAD work on a Foreign Object Debris (FOD) closeout system that interfaces with numerous other vehicle systems, designing an adaptable layout to accommodate future changes.
Designed avionics mounting and tooling brackets.
Contributed to Design for Manufacturability (DFM) changes across the Aft, Header Tank, and Prop Hardware assemblies.
Worked within a team of various disciplines to design example content to best teach basic robotics principles.
Developed mechanical lessons for an adaptable middle school robotics curriculum built around an existing kit of parts.

Led a group of students to design and iterate the intake, end effector, and shooter mechanisms across three competition seasons on a team that has qualified for the FIRST Championship every year and won multiple district events.
Ran multi-user CAD and version control in SOLIDWORKS PDM and Onshape to keep a large student design team working against a single robot assembly.
Cut aluminum, polycarbonate, and composite parts on CNC machinery using Fusion CAM.
Coordinated and developed the competition strategy used by the team during events.
Developed an Angular-based website to efficiently process and display scouting data, improving data accessibility for the team.
Worked with teams from around the world to develop effective competition strategies.
Used SOLIDWORKS to design a competitive robot with a 3 DoF arm.

awards.title: Charles O. Thompson Scholar
awards.summary: Awarded for outstanding academic achievement in the first year.

projects.name: RBE 3000s - 4 DOF Inverse Kinematics, ROS 2, and Autonomous Navigation
projects.description: Manipulator kinematics, computer vision pick-and-place, and autonomous navigation on a TurtleBot3.
highlights: Derived and implemented full forward/inverse kinematics (DH parameterization) and a velocity Jacobian for a 4-DOF manipulator (OpenManipulator-X) in MATLAB, validated against a custom interactive 3D model.

Built a computer vision pick-and-place pipeline: intrinsic/extrinsic camera calibration, HSV color segmentation, centroid detection, and a geometric height-correction model to autonomously sort colored spheres into bins.

Designed a layered ROS 2 software architecture combining a Behavior Tree for mission control with a Finite State Machine for navigation and a request-reply Dispatcher node to complete multi-stop delivery tasks with obstacle-triggered replanning.
Implemented A* path planning with configuration-space obstacle inflation and risk-weighted costing, plus frontier-based SLAM exploration and particle-filter re-localization, on a TurtleBot3 in ROS 2.

projects.name: IQP - Honolulu Bike Share Network Optimization
projects.description: Interactive Qualifying Project with Secure Bike Share in Honolulu, HI.
highlights: Built ArcGIS Pro suitability models layering census, transit, and bike-lane data to identify expansion sites, paired with a ridership-weighted station ranking to flag relocation candidates for the system operator.

Designed a demographically conditioned user survey distributed through the operator's 20,000-person mailing list under IRB approval, analyzing 233 responses to isolate infrastructure quality and bike supply as the dominant barriers to ridership.

Authored the team's final technical report and client-facing improvement plan, including a matched control-group methodology for measuring the effect of QR way-finding signage on bus-to-bike transfers.

projects.name: RBE 2000s - Sensors and Actuators
projects.description: Embedded control, actuation, and structural analysis coursework.
highlights: Analyzed stress and structural integrity using SOLIDWORKS FEA.
Applied inverse kinematics to control a double-jointed arm in order to draw different images and move to different points.
Controlled servos and brushed/brushless motors with ESCs, read encoder feedback, and built custom embedded circuits on Arduino and Raspberry Pi Pico.
Used a custom library to control a two-wheeled robot autonomously using various sensors.

projects.name: ES 3011 - Novel Car Control Project
projects.description: Applied classical control theory to a custom-bodied payload-carrying vehicle.
highlights: Tuned PID parameters to carry a stack of 6 blocks through straight-line and 90-degree turn courses.
Designed the custom vehicle body, streamlining electronics mounting for the design bonus.

projects.name: RBE 1001 - Autonomous Fruit Picking Robot
projects.description: Collaborated with a team to create a small autonomous robot to collect and deliver 3D printed 'fruit'.
highlights: Designed and programmed a four bar, elevator, and unconventional drive train using cameras, gyros, and encoder feedback driven by state machines.
Designed and 3D printed parts to interface with a given kit of parts.
